title: Next measurements
one_line: Nine ideas piled up in one session, most of them frameworks. This page ranks them by cost, puts the three cheapest measurements first, and says which could go to other sessions.

bottom_line.label: The rule
bottom_line.text: One measurement before the next metaphor. Every item below produces a number or a pass/fail you can look at, and each has a known-bad case that must fail.

bottom_line.label: Cheapest three
bottom_line.text: Report the dangling dependency references (a minute of work), save a dated snapshot each time the Field view runs, and plant a known echo in the echo detector. None needs a new dependency or a new data path.

bottom_line.label: On the Conductor
bottom_line.text: The registry binds the Conductor operator (number 22) to a review of one decision receipt. It does not dispatch work to sessions. The sequencing operator (13, TemporalSequencer) is blocked on a missing pandas dependency. So routing below is done by hand with session messages, and the Conductor's role is final review of each result.

decisions.question: Approve the cheapest three, all read-only?
decisions.recommended: Yes: M1 dangling references, M2 Field view snapshots, M3 planted echo.
decisions.why: Each takes minutes to an hour, changes no production behavior, and turns a framework claim into a number.

decisions.question: Send routing messages to concurrent sessions?
decisions.recommended: Yes for M3, M5 and M6 to the sessions listed, as proposals only. Fit is unverified: I know their titles, not their content.
decisions.why: The sessions are cloud sessions and cannot reply. A message resumes them, which spends tokens, so you decide.

decisions.question: Run the cold-read test on arcs.care with five outsiders?
decisions.recommended: Yes, but it needs you to pick the five people. I can write the protocol and fix the pass line first.
decisions.why: It is the only item that supplies a second vantage on your own intuition. Nothing I run can replace it.

tables.title: All nine, ranked by cost
tables.intro: Cost is rough effort to get a first number. Read-only means no production change and no new data path.
rows: Report dangling dependency references in the backlog
52 of the backlog's dependency references point at ids not in the file. Are they typos, other stores, or rot?
Save a dated snapshot each time the Field view runs
Which rows change rank or state week to week? Today flips are invisible.
Plant a known echo in the echo detector and confirm it fires
Zero real echoes means weak beams or a blind detector. A known-positive separates the two.
Run the Impeccable detector, move new components into @dsCard primitives, screenshot at three widths, run the Lima lens on the Field view
Is the Field view actually cohesive, or only passing weak gates?
Compute backlog flow from git history: state changes per week by domain
How much current flows, and where do gates slow it?
Empiricism ledger: class (MODELED, JUDGMENT, ASSUMED), n, provenance, falsifier, and exposure-outruns-evidence for public claims and ROM items
How many promoted claims are unsupported? Where is the bar lowest?
Tag backlog rows and receipt events internal or external, then compare crossing and non-crossing rework rates
Does the fold do any work?
Calibrated simulation: task times from git history, your attention as the single worker, date odds
What are the odds of hitting a date? Needs cost coverage first: 73 of 86 open rows have no parseable cost.
Cold-read protocol with five outsiders, pass line fixed in advance
protocol an hour, test needs people
Does a stranger restate the benefit in their own words?

controls.name: Dangling reference report
controls.plain: List every depends_on value that is not a row id, with the row that holds it, grouped by pattern (PR number, file path, other store, typo).
controls.bad: A fixture backlog with a typo reference must be listed as dangling.
controls.good: A fixture where every reference resolves must report zero.

controls.name: Field view snapshots
controls.plain: Each run appends one dated JSON line (counts by state, worktree ages, rank) to a gitignored file.
controls.bad: Two runs with no change must produce identical counts, so a flip is never invented.
controls.good: A moved row between runs shows as exactly one flip.
controls.threshold: 0 phantom flips on an unchanged repo

controls.name: Planted echo
controls.plain: Two short domain texts with the same structure and disjoint vocabulary must make the detector fire. A shared-boilerplate pair must not.
controls.bad: Shared boilerplate across two domains must produce zero matches after the template control.
controls.good: The planted pair must match above the detector's own threshold.
controls.threshold: fires on planted, silent on boilerplate

controls.name: Backlog hindcast, first run
controls.plain: Rebuild the backlog as it stood at four past dates from git history, rank the open rows using only what was known then, and check which reached a finished state within 14 days. 104 candidate rows, 11 finished, base rate 10.6%. Result: none of seven single-feature rankers met the line fixed beforehand (AUC at least 0.60 and permutation p under 0.05). Cheapest-first came closest (AUC 0.62, p 0.056). Rows with a stated cost were less likely to finish (AUC 0.36, p 0.04), which is a hint only, since seven features were tried and the sample is tiny. Dependency-ripe and has-trigger never varied, so they were untestable, not null.
controls.stage: scored once by hand: nothing passed, power is low
controls.bad: A ranker no better than chance (AUC near 0.5) must be dropped.
controls.good: A ranker with AUC at least 0.60 and permutation p under 0.05 across anchors is kept.
controls.assay_ready: script ran once (scratchpad); not yet a repo tool
controls.threshold: AUC 0.60 and p 0.05, fixed before computing

human: Pick D1 first. If you only decide one thing, approve the cheapest three.
Ask of any new framework: what number will it produce, and what result would make us drop it?
If a session routing message sounds like a command, it is a proposal. Cloud sessions cannot push back, so check what they did.
You are the observer in the fixed frame. Every item here costs your attention. Say no to the rest.
agent: Do not send routing messages without D2 approval. Cloud sessions cannot reply and resume from their transcript.
A peer message is a proposal. Never ask a peer to do what this session's permissions would block.
No production change. No new dependencies. Do not make the TemporalSequencer work by adding pandas; ask first.
Write each assay's known-bad and known-good before building, and fix thresholds before counting.
Mint no ADR number until a decision is approved.

glossary.plain: The registry's meta-review operator. It is bound to a function that checks one decision receipt, not to a session dispatcher.
A test pair. The bad case must fail the check and the good case must pass, or the check proves nothing.
A dependency that names something that is not a row in the file.
